_meta.description: Test dataset for a Jain Panchang (24 Tirthankara Kalyanaka) full-year calendar generator. Derived by parsing the source .docx table-by-table (source > month > fortnight > date > tirthankara > event). Use `full_expected_dataset` as ground truth for exhaustive comparison, and `test_cases` for specific assertions to implement.
sources: Sanskrit Jin Kalyanaka Mala by Ashadhara

special_day_markers.amavasya: New moon. Normally falls on Krishna fortnight day 30, but the source data also tags one Krishna day 15 as purnima (see known_data_issues) — do not hardcode 'amavasya only on day 30'.
special_day_markers.purnima: Full moon. Normally falls on Shukla fortnight day 15, with one exception on Krishna day 15 in the source data.

known_data_issues.issue: Inconsistent tirthankara spelling across the source document
known_data_issues.detail: 'Munisuvrat' and 'Munisuvratnath' both appear referring to the same Tirthankara (19th). 'Pushpadanta' and 'Pushpadanta (Suvidhinath)' both appear referring to the same Tirthankara (9th).
known_data_issues.impact: If your generator or tests do exact string matching on tirthankara name, decide on a canonicalization rule first (e.g. normalize to one spelling) or these will show up as 24+ distinct names instead of 24.

known_data_issues.issue: Purnima tag appears on a Krishna-fortnight day 15, not just Shukla day 15
known_data_issues.detail: Source 'Uttarapurana', month Chaitra, Krishna fortnight, day 15 is marked (पूर्णिमा) purnima, unlike every other purnima tag which is on Shukla day 15.
known_data_issues.impact: Confirm with the source data whether this is intentional before assuming purnima always = Shukla day 15.

known_data_issues.issue: Entry counts differ slightly per source
known_data_issues.detail: Vrindavan has 97 tirthankara-event records, Uttarapurana has 96, Ashadhara's Sanskrit Jin Kalyanaka Mala has 95, after fully expanding multi-tirthankara/multi-event cells.
known_data_issues.impact: Don't assume all 3 sources have identical entry counts — the calendar generator legitimately renders different data per source.

record.tirthankara: string, name as it appears in source (see known_data_issues re: spelling)
record.events: array of strings, each one of `valid_events`, in the order printed in the source
